What happens to drilling fluid after the bore is complete?
Most drilling fluid is a liquid slurry. It’s a mix of water, suspended clay, and cuttings. When you dispose of it, it’s treated as liquid waste.

This liquid waste stream is difficult to manage. It requires specific handling and often means multiple truck runs to a disposal site.

The physical principle is simple. If you can force the suspended solids to bind together, the free water separates out. What’s left behind is a stable, solid cake.

This process changes the waste from a liquid problem to a manageable, stackable solid. It’s the same principle that lets wet soil firm up as it dries.

Turning liquid waste into a solid stackable cake.
When you finish a bore, the disposal waste is often a liquid slurry. This creates site headaches and adds disposal costs.

Eco Dry changes the game. It uses a simple chemical process to solidify the fluid waste. It binds the suspended solids and separates the free water.

The result is a stable, solid cake that can be stacked on a pallet. This drastically reduces the volume and the number of truck runs needed for disposal.

If your site has tight access or sensitive ground, using Eco Dry helps the crew finish faster and keeps the contractor looking good on the next job.
Need to dial in a waste program for your next site? Give the team a call.
